{{Quote|I'm starting to think I shouldn't have come anywhere near this place...|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="fury" />}}
'''Garn''' was a desolate [[Planet/Legends|world]] of craggy rocks and [[Death/Legends|dead]] [[Tree/Legends|trees]] shrouded in a dense yellow fog, located in the [[Cadma sector/Legends|Cadma sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. The planet was once home to the [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-wielding order known as the [[Order of the Terrible Glare/Legends|Order of the Terrible Glare]] thousands of years before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], until the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] laid waste to Garn at the climax of a [[Pius Dea Crusades|war]] between the two organizations. Although the Terrible Glare was completely wiped out, their [[High Shaman of the Terrible Glare|High Shaman]], [[Rur/Legends|Rur]], preserved an aspect of his consciousness by uploading his personality to a [[Computer/Legends|computer system]] in his citadel on ruined Garn. A vengeful Rur lured a number of passing [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to their demise with false distress calls over a period of thousands of years, until aspiring Jedi [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] broke the news that the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] had destroyed the Jedi Order&mdash;unable to comprehend that his vengeance was out of reach, the remnants of Rur's mind self-destructed.<ref name="fury" />

==Behind the scenes==
Garn was the setting of "[[Blind Fury!]]," a [[1982]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] story appearing in [[Star Wars Monthly 159|''Star Wars Monthly'' 159]], written by [[Alan Moore]] and illustrated by [[John Stokes]].<ref name="fury" />
